POLICY.text: Land use and all modes of transport are integrated, and the adverse effects of traffic generation on the network are managed.
An integrated transport network including public transport, walking, cycling, private vehicles and freight is provided for.
Pedestrian safety and amenity along public footpaths is prioritised.
Road/rail crossings operate safely with neighbouring land use and development.

Development generating trips with potentially more than minor effects, outside the City Centre, Metropolitan Centre, Town Centre and THAB zones and the Centre Fringe Office Control, manages its effects and integrates with the network (travel planning, alternatives to car trips, staging, local improvements).
Major proposals for discretionary consent prepare an integrated transport assessment covering pedestrians, cyclists, public transport users, freight and motorists.

D1.title: Screening status
D1.place: Title page, every report page footer and every CSV export
D1.text: Spare Construct is a browser-based sketch and screening tool. It is not an approved regional transport model and it is not the Auckland Forecasting Centre Macro Strategic Model (MSM). Its results are indicative and are intended to scope, test and support a transport assessment. They must be reviewed, and where necessary confirmed with approved tools, by a suitably qualified transport planner or traffic engineer before they are relied on in any resource consent, plan change, notice of requirement, Fast-track application or funding decision.

D2.title: Expert evidence
D2.text: Spare Construct is not an expert witness and does not give opinions. Any person who relies on these outputs in evidence remains responsible for complying with the Code of Conduct for Expert Witnesses (Environment Court Practice Note 2023, section 9), including stating the assumptions and data relied on, the uncertainty in the results, and appropriate sensitivity and uncertainty analyses for any model. This report is DRAFT until adopted and signed by a named, suitably qualified author.

D3.title: Junction results
D3.text: Junction delay, degree of saturation, level of service and queue results are calculated by Spare Construct using HCM 6 / Akcelik-based methods. They are indicative and are not SIDRA output. Any junction result relied on for a consent decision, signal design (ATOC Traffic Signals Design Guidelines) or condition should be confirmed in SIDRA or another tool accepted by the road controlling authority.

D4.title: Economics
D4.place: Every economic table and the IPM panel
D4.text: The benefit-cost ratio is an indicative screening estimate following NZTA Monetised Benefits and Costs Manual v1.7.5 conventions. It is equivalent to an Indicative Efficiency Rating, not a funding-approval BCR. It is not MBCM-compliant unless the full procedures are applied to a model calibrated and validated to the NZTA Transport Model Development Guidelines and independently reviewed. IPM efficiency bands for 2027-30 are shown from NZTA's initial draft (August 2026) and may change after GPS 2027.

D5.title: ANOP
D5.text: ANOP levels of service are indicative Spare Construct estimates. Confirm them in Auckland Transport's ANOP Assessment Tool using AT speed data before relying on them.

D6.title: Calibration
D6.text: Calibration and validation statistics are reported against the NZTA Transport Model Development Guidelines (2019) for the stated model purpose category. Those criteria are not a pass/fail checklist, and meeting them does not by itself make a model fit for purpose. Fitness for purpose is a judgment for the analyst and peer reviewer and, where NZTA is involved, NZTA's modelling specialists.

D7.title: Regional consistency
D7.text: The AT ITA Guidelines 2025 v2 expect detailed modelling to be consistent with regional MSM forecasts where appropriate. Where this report states that MSM consistency was not checked, the forecasts should be reconciled with MSM or Auckland Forecasting Centre outputs before lodgement for any proposal with network-wide effects.

D8.title: Safety
D8.text: Crash histories are taken from NZTA CAS and the most recent months may be incomplete. Spare Construct's safety screening and audit briefing pack support, but do not replace, a Safe System Audit by an independent, qualified specialist, or sight distance assessment to Austroads Guide to Road Design Part 4A.

D9.title: Speed limits
D9.text: This cost benefit disclosure statement follows the structure of clause 3.3 of the Land Transport Rule: Setting of Speed Limits 2024. It is not an MBCM benefit-cost ratio and cannot be used in place of MBCM procedures for NLTF funding.

D10.title: Regulatory currency
D10.text: Statutory references reflect the law and guidance as at [version date] for the pathway and lodgement date shown. Under the Planning Act 2026, consents lodged before 30 October 2026 are processed under the RMA as it stood immediately before 30 September 2026, and those lodged later are processed under the amended RMA as at lodgement. The specified transition date to the new planning system has not been set. This report is not legal or planning advice. Confirm the applicable provisions at lodgement.

D11.title: Authorities
D11.text: Since 7 May 2026 Auckland Council is the road controlling authority for Auckland roads (Local Government (Auckland Council) Act 2009 s47), with local boards exercising specified powers on local and collector roads and Auckland Transport continuing as the transport CCO for public transport. AUP provisions that still refer to Auckland Transport are quoted as written. Confirm the reviewing and approving body for this application.

D12.title: Hand-over
D12.text: This export is prepared for use in [SIDRA / SATURN / Aimsun / AT ANOP tool / NZTA IER tool / MBCM workbook / Safe System Audit / NZTA access application]. Results produced in that tool, not the Spare Construct estimates, should be reported where the tool is required or accepted by the reviewing authority.

D13.title: Assumed thresholds
D13.place: Any value marked Spare Construct assumption
D13.text: Values marked "Spare Construct assumption" are Spare Construct defaults, not published rules. Agree them with the reviewing authority at scoping or replace them with project-specific values.
